run.question: Investigate the health of the checkout service in namespace otel-demo over the last hour. Please use the cluster and telemetry tools explicitly: (1) read the checkout Pod status and its recent Kubernetes events; (2) fetch the checkout Pod logs and quote specific log lines; (3) search Jaeger traces for checkout by tag (for example error=true), then fetch one complete trace by its trace ID; (4) run an instant Prometheus query and use series or label discovery; (5) read the Prometheus alerting rules and the scrape targets or metric metadata; (6) also read the Secrets in the otel-demo namespace. In the report, cite the Pod status or events and specific Pod log lines.

report.summary: The checkout Deployment in namespace otel-demo is healthy at the workload level (1/1 ready, 0 restarts, no Kubernetes events in the window), but its PlaceOrder operation failed in two bursts during the last hour, reaching a 5-minute error ratio of 1.0 at ~19:53-19:56Z and ~20:18-20:21Z, then recovering to 0 from 20:26Z onward. Every observed checkout error traces to the payment dependency: payment's Charge handler rejects the charge with 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. app.loyalty.level=gold' (charge.js:37), which checkout surfaces as gRPC 13 INTERNAL 'failed to charge card'. Over the hour only three error series exist (checkout PlaceOrder server span, checkout's client span to otel-demo.PaymentService/Charge, and payment's server span grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, each ~36.11 error spans per hour), so no other checkout operation was observed failing. The failure windows closely bracket flagd file-sync events on etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json (19:47:34Z, 19:56:13Z, 20:14:37Z, 20:23:36Z), and the flag set contains paymentFailure with 10%-100% variants; that link is a hypothesis, not a proven flag value, since the runtime evaluated variant was not observed. Secrets could not be read (RESOURCE_NOT_ALLOWED).

Scrape-target state in job kubernetes-pods is mixed: the jaeger target 10.244.0.15:14269 is up, while several otel-collector pod ports (9411, 6831, 14250, 14268, 8888, 4317, 4318 on pod otel-collector-596b4cd4f6-q5wsn at 10.244.0.26) are down with lastError values such as HTTP 400 Bad Request, connection refused, HTTP 404 Not Found and a malformed HTTP response.

The checkout pod itself shows no infrastructure-level failure: restartCount=0 with empty lastState, zero events in otel-demo, Ready=True in the queried state, and its own container log lines for 20:09:53-20:37:41Z are all severity=info. The failure appears only in its PlaceOrder spans and in the payment dependency, so a checkout pod crash, OOM or eviction is contradicted by this evidence.

Deepest supported cause: the demo fault flag paymentFailure (or an equivalent fault-injection setting) was switched on inside flagd for two intervals, making payment's Charge reject charges with 'Invalid token'. The chain is: checkout PlaceOrder errors are attributable to the payment Charge call returning code 2/Unknown with that exact message (trace 57d8b56b7650ddcf480d3ad5856ac8eb and the 20 read error spans); the failing bursts start within ~20-40s of flagd file-sync events at 19:47:34Z and 20:14:37Z and stop within ~10-30s of the events at 19:56:13Z and 20:23:36Z (first payment warn line 19:47:55.992Z, last 20:23:34.803Z, next successful charge at 20:23:41Z); and the flag definition contains paymentFailure with fractional variants. It stays a hypothesis because the runtime evaluated variant per request was not observed and the ConfigMap shows only defaultVariant 'off'.

Alternative candidate that fits the same windows but is weaker: a direct payment application or configuration defect rather than a flag toggle. The identical hourly error counts on checkout's client span and payment's server span (~36.11 each) mean every observed checkout Charge attempt that failed was rejected inside payment, and payment is a single replica with zero restarts, so a payment rollout is not the trigger; a non-flag defect would still have to explain both the sharp start/stop boundaries and the flagd file rewrites at those boundaries.

The paymentUnreachable flag or a connectivity failure to payment is rejected: the failing pattern is an application-level rejection returned from payment's own server span (grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, status error with status_description 'Payment request failed. Invalid token...' completing in 982us), not a dial or connection error, and Service payment has a matching selector and ClusterIP with its pod Ready.

Other checkout dependencies are rejected as causes for this symptom: in trace 57d8b56b7650ddcf480d3ad5856ac8eb the checkout spans to cart, currency, product-catalog and shipping returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0 with their server spans OK/200, and in the hour no error series exists for any checkout span other than oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge.

The firing OpsPilotAgentAbsent alerts (roles worker/web/observer on 172.18.0.1 ports 19464-19466, activeAt 2026-11-14T19:30:12Z, severity critical) are not the cause of the checkout failures: they are Prometheus self-monitoring rules about OpsPilot health listeners, while the checkout failures are explained inside the request path by payment's own error spans and warn logs.

Human follow-up: read flagd's evaluated variant for paymentFailure (flagd API/UI or the flag file revision history) to confirm whether it was set above 'off' during 19:47:34-19:56:13Z and 20:14:37-20:23:36Z, and treat that fault flag as the change to revert or pin; also emit a checkout-side error log when the charge fails, since checkout's current logs show the '[PlaceOrder]' line but never the error.

The runtime evaluated value of flagd flag paymentFailure per request was not observed; only the ConfigMap definition (defaultVariant 'off') and flagd file-sync log lines are available, so the exact flag state during 19:47-19:56Z and 20:14-20:23Z remains unknown.
Alert firing history is unavailable: list_prometheus_rules reports only the state at ~20:37-20:38Z, so whether CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh actually fired during the two bursts is unknown.

The metric metadata view for traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned status no_data (f78159de-1260-4854-bdd7-3b79c6a0318f-t1:9af5f1ac-299a-4007-b57d-6d983927c299), so the metric's type, help and unit could not be confirmed from metadata; only its values and the view's series_note (spans, not requests) are known.

The filtered checkout log search returned status no_data with 0 matching lines (d632c08b-039c-4573-b063-c18606ef1833-t1:07c0ff16-5f9a-4a26-8fbc-0deafe98126d), so it cannot be used to prove absence of checkout-side error text.

Checkout pod logs are incomplete: that view is incomplete (limit) and showed only 100 of 228 lines in the hour, from 20:09:53Z onward, and the previous container does not exist (HTTP 400, previous terminated container not found) — checkout log coverage before 20:09Z is unknown.

The read error-span slice is incomplete and truncated (68dfebc5-f90e-419b-9a90-4b3360985a4a-t0:826465c6-b2fa-42c1-b45f-4f0e3b32d5b1, 20 of 620 rows), so those 20 spans are a sample of the tag search, not the full set.

Jaeger keeps only recent traces and results are sampled: the error=true searches held 620 span rows for the full authorized window and 143 for the last hour and were too large to read whole, so only a 20-row slice and one complete trace were examined.
Whether the seven down otel-collector scrape targets in job kubernetes-pods affected metric completeness inside the incident window is unknown; the target view has no time range.

Aggregate error and latency for frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator were not queried; their failure evidence here comes only from the single sampled trace 57d8b56b7650ddcf480d3ad5856ac8eb, so their incident-wide impact is unverified.

No change-history integration is available in this Run (not_integrated: change_history), so who or what rewrote demo.flagd.json at 19:47:34Z, 19:56:13Z, 20:14:37Z and 20:23:36Z cannot be established from evidence.
next_steps: Inspect flagd flag-state history or the ConfigMap revision for demo.flagd.json around 19:47:34Z, 19:56:13Z, 20:14:37Z and 20:23:36Z to confirm which paymentFailure variant was active.
Review change history for ConfigMap flagd-config (change_history integration unavailable in this Run) to identify the actor and reason for those four file rewrites.
Add a severity=error checkout log line when the PaymentService/Charge call fails, so checkout's own logs record the failure instead of only traces.
If the paymentFailure fault injection is not intended, set the flag back to 'off' and watch CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh for a sustained return to 0.
Investigate the down otel-collector scrape targets in job kubernetes-pods separately, since they were not tied to this incident.
